patches.name: Drag
patches.summary: Lets people drag a layer around and outputs where it should be, with optional bounds, axis lock, and momentum.
patches.docs:
## How it works
Drag watches for a finger or mouse pressing on **Layer** and turns the movement into a **Position**. It doesn't move anything by itself: link Position into the layer's Position property.

- **Start Position** is where the layer sits before anyone drags it, and where **Reset** (a pulse, a signal that's on for one frame) puts it back.
- **Axis** limits dragging to horizontal or vertical movement.
- **Clip** keeps Position between **Min** and **Max** (both in the parent's coordinates).
- **Momentum** lets a flicked layer keep gliding after release. **Momentum Friction** controls how soon it stops: 50 feels like iOS scrolling, 250 stops quickly.
- **Dragging** is true while a finger is on the layer, and **Velocity** reports speed in points per second.

Layer can be a different layer than the one you move, so a small handle can drag a whole panel.

## Tips
- To snap somewhere on release, feed Position into a Spring Animation with Dragging as Gesture Active and Velocity as Gesture Velocity.
- For a slider, set Axis to Horizontal, turn on Clip, and use Min and Max for the track ends.

## Coming from Origami
Drag Settings is built in: Clip, Min, Max, Momentum, and Momentum Friction are advanced inputs on Drag. Sonobe adds Axis, Dragging, and Velocity. Positions use a top-left origin with y pointing down. Until the first drag, Position follows Start Position live, so editing it updates the viewer.

inputs.description: The layer whose touches start a drag; empty means a press anywhere on the screen drags.

inputs.description: When on, the layer can be dragged; when off, presses are ignored and Position holds.

inputs.name: Start Position
inputs.description: Where Position starts, in the parent's points from its top-left; Reset returns here.

inputs.name: Reset
inputs.description: Pulse to put the layer back at Start Position and stop any movement.

inputs.name: Axis

enumOptions.description: Drag freely in any direction.

enumOptions.name: Vertical
enumOptions.description: Only y changes.

inputs.name: Clip
inputs.description: When on, Position always stays between Min and Max.

inputs.name: Min
inputs.description: Smallest allowed Position (the top-left corner of the drag bounds) when Clip is on.

inputs.name: Max
inputs.description: Largest allowed Position (the bottom-right corner of the drag bounds) when Clip is on.

inputs.name: Momentum
inputs.description: When on, a flicked layer keeps gliding after release and slows down by Momentum Friction.

inputs.name: Momentum Friction
inputs.description: How quickly a flicked layer slows down, 0 to 950: 50 feels like iOS scrolling, 950 stops almost at once.

outputs.name: Position

outputs.description: How fast Position is changing, in points per second, while dragging or gliding; 0 at rest.

commonMistakes: Nothing moves when you drag: Drag only computes a position. Link Position into the layer's Position property.
The layer jumps or drifts on the first drag: Start Position doesn't match where the layer is drawn. Set Start Position to the layer's authored position.
The layer won't move at all with Clip on: Min and Max are equal or leave no room. Min and Max bound Position itself (the anchor point), not the layer's edges.

examples.title: Drag a card anywhere
examples.outline:
layer card rectangle "Card" @16,120 160x220 position←move_card.position
patch move_card drag layer=@card startPosition=[16,120]

examples.title: Slide a knob along a track
examples.description: Axis and Clip keep the knob on the track; Momentum lets a flick glide to the end.

patch slide drag layer=@knob startPosition=[40,400] axis=horizontal clip=true min=[18,400] max=[340,400] momentum=true momentumFriction=250

patches.name: Scroll
patches.summary: Scrolls a content layer inside its parent with momentum, rubber banding, or paging, and outputs the scroll position and page.
patches.docs:
## How it works
Scroll turns drags, flicks, and mouse-wheel scrolling on **Layer** into a **Position** for that layer. The layer's parent is the visible window: content bigger than the parent can scroll, and the parent's Clip Contents hides what's outside. Link Position into the content layer's Position.

- **Scroll X** and **Scroll Y** choose Off, Free (momentum and rubber banding), or Paging (snap page by page) for each direction.
- **Start Position** is where the content sits when it's scrolled all the way to the top-left.
- **X** and **Y** are the same position split into numbers, for scroll-linked effects like collapsing headers. They go negative as content moves up or left.
- **Page X** and **Page Y** count pages from 0.
- **Dragging** is true while a finger is scrolling; **Moving** stays true until the content settles.

Advanced inputs set the content size, page size and padding, direction locking, deceleration, rubber banding, and jumps (pulses that scroll to a position).

## Tips
- Put the content in a group sized to the visible area, with Clip Contents on.
- For cards narrower than the screen, set Page Size to the card size and Page Padding to the gap.

## Coming from Origami
Scroll Settings is built in as advanced inputs. Link Position instead of wiring X and Y into separate position fields. Sonobe adds Start Position, Rubber Band, Dragging, Moving, and mouse-wheel scrolling. Coordinates start at the parent's top-left with y down.

patches.name: Mouse
patches.summary: Reports the mouse pointer's position, which buttons are held, and how fast the scroll wheel or trackpad is scrolling.
patches.docs:
## How it works
Mouse listens to the mouse across the whole prototype, not a particular layer.

- **Position** is where the pointer is, in points from the prototype's top-left, even while no button is pressed.
- **Left**, **Right**, and **Middle** are true while that button is held.
- **Scroll Velocity** is how fast the wheel or trackpad is scrolling, in points per second. **Scroll Delta** is how far it scrolled this frame. Both are positive when scrolling toward the bottom or right of a page.

On phones and tablets a finger acts like the left button, and there's no wheel.

## Tips
- For clicks or hovering on one layer, use Interaction or Hover instead.
- To move content with the wheel, subtract Scroll Delta from its position each frame, or use Scroll, which already handles the wheel.
- Smooth Value makes a custom cursor trail the pointer gently.

## Coming from Origami
Origami's older docs list Down and Location; current files use Left, Right, Middle, Position, and Scroll Velocity, which Sonobe matches. Position starts at the top-left with y down instead of the viewer center, and Scroll Velocity is per second instead of per frame. Scroll Delta is new.

outputs.name: Position
outputs.description: Where the mouse pointer is, in points from the prototype's top-left; keeps its last value when the pointer leaves.

outputs.name: Left
outputs.description: True while the left mouse button (or a finger) is pressed.

outputs.name: Right
outputs.description: True while the right mouse button is pressed.

outputs.name: Middle
outputs.description: True while the middle mouse button (the wheel) is pressed.

outputs.name: Scroll Velocity
outputs.description: How fast the wheel or trackpad is scrolling, in points per second; positive toward the bottom and right.

outputs.name: Scroll Delta
outputs.description: How far the wheel or trackpad scrolled this frame, in points; [0, 0] when it isn't scrolling.

commonMistakes: Clicks register anywhere on the screen: Mouse is global. Use Interaction with a layer for clicks on one element.
A wheel-driven layer moves the wrong way: Scroll Delta is positive when scrolling down a page. Subtract it from the layer's position instead of adding it.
Right never turns on in the browser: the browser's context menu takes the click. Test in the desktop app, or check that nothing else handles right clicks on the page.

examples.title: A custom cursor that follows the mouse
examples.outline:
layer cursor oval "Cursor" 24x24 anchor=[0.5,0.5] position←pointer.position
patch pointer mouse

examples.title: Right-click to open a menu
examples.description: Right turns the menu on and a left click closes it; Turn Off wins when both happen in one frame.
examples.outline:
layer menu rectangle "Menu" @120,200 180x220 enabled←menu_open.on
patch pointer mouse
patch menu_open switch turnOn←pointer.right turnOff←pointer.left

patches.name: Touches
patches.summary: Lists every finger touching the screen or a layer as loops of positions and pressures, for multi-touch effects.
patches.docs:
## How it works
Touches reports every finger currently pressed, as **loops** (lists that make a patch or layer repeat once per item).

- **Positions** holds one point per finger, in points from the prototype's top-left. Link it to a layer's Position to draw one copy of the layer under each finger.
- **Pressures** holds how hard each finger presses, from 0 to 1.
- **IDs** gives each finger a number that stays the same until it lifts.
- **Count** is how many fingers are down.
- **JSON** has the same data as a list of objects, handy for debugging.

Leave **Layer** empty to watch the whole screen, or pick a layer to count only touches that started on it.

## Tips
- A mouse is one pointer. Test multi-touch on a phone with the web player.
- Fingers are listed in the order they touched. When one lifts, the fingers after it move up a place; use IDs to follow a particular finger.
- Most screens and mice can't sense pressure and report a fixed value.

## Coming from Origami
Origami outputs one JSON structure; Sonobe outputs typed loops plus a JSON output for compatibility. Positions start at the top-left with y down, and Pressure runs 0 to 1 instead of Force 0 to 6.67. Layer and Enabled are new.
patches.behavior:
Stateless (the pointer tracker owns touch identity).

Each frame:
```
if (!enabled) { emit empty loops, count 0, json []; return; }
const touches = pressedPointers(layerRef)       // pointers whose press hit chain contains the layer
  .sort((a, b) => a.startTime - b.startTime || a.id - b.id);
ctx.output("positions", loop(touches.map((t) => t.position)));
ctx.output("pressures", loop(touches.map((t) => t.pressure ?? 1)));
ctx.output("ids", loop(touches.map((t) => t.id)));
ctx.output("count", touches.length);
ctx.output("json", touches.map((t) => ({ id: t.id, position: [t.position[0], t.position[1]], pressure: t.pressure ?? 1 })));
```

- Which touches: a pointer counts from the frame its `down` event is processed until the frame of its `up` or `cancel`, where it's already gone. With Layer empty, every pressed pointer counts. With a layer, a pointer counts when the layer or one of its descendants was in the press hit chain (touches bubble, ARCHITECTURE.md §5.5); moving off the layer doesn't remove it. Hovering mice aren't touches.
- Order: by press time, ties broken by pointer id. Indices shift down when an earlier finger lifts; IDs are the `pointerId` from `InputEvent` and never change during a touch.
- Pressure: the event's `pressure` (0 to 1) from the latest down or move event; `1` when an event carries none. Mice commonly report 0.5.
- Contract gap: `PointerSnapshot` exposes only the first pointer's position plus `pointerCount`. Proposed: `RuntimeServices.pointers(layer: LayerRef | null): { id: number; position: [number, number]; pressure: number; startTime: number }[]`, backed by `PointerTracker`'s active records. Until it lands, output a single-item loop from `pointer(layerRef)` while `down` (pressure 1, id 0) and use `pointerCount` for Count.
- Loops: outputs are whole loops (`wholeLoop`). An empty set of touches outputs empty loops, which replicate a linked layer zero times. The inputs don't loop: a looped Layer uses its first item and warns once per restart.
- Frame 0: no touches; empty loops and Count 0.
- Edge cases: a missing or deleted layer matches no touches. Non-finite coordinates from an event are ignored.
- Disabled: empty loops, Count 0, JSON `[]`.
- Muted: the same idle values as Disabled.
- Platform and simulation: phones and tablets report every finger; desktop mice report one pointer while a button is held. In headless simulation, `pointer` InputEvents with distinct `pointerId`s simulate fingers.
- Evaluation: `alwaysEvaluate`.
- Restart and dispose: nothing to reset or release.

inputs.description: Only count touches that started on this layer or its children; empty counts every touch on the screen.

inputs.name: Enabled
inputs.description: When on, touches are reported; when off, every output is empty.

outputs.name: Positions
outputs.description: A loop with each finger's position, in points from the prototype's top-left.

outputs.name: Pressures
outputs.description: A loop with how hard each finger presses, 0 (lightest) to 1 (hardest).

outputs.name: IDs
outputs.description: A loop with each finger's id, which stays the same until that finger lifts.

outputs.name: Count
outputs.description: How many fingers are touching right now.

outputs.name: JSON
outputs.description: The same touches as a JSON array of { id, position, pressure } objects.

commonMistakes: Only one dot ever appears: you're testing with a mouse, which is a single pointer. Open the web player on a phone to try several fingers.
A dot jumps to another finger when one lifts: positions are listed in touch order, so indices shift. Use IDs to follow a specific finger.

patches.name: Pop Switch
patches.summary: Swipes or pinches a value between two states, then springs to the nearer one and reports whether it's on.
patches.docs:
## How it works
Pop Switch is a switch you control with a gesture. While a finger swipes or pinches **Layer**, **Output** follows it. On release, Output springs to **Start** (off) or **End** (on), whichever the flick was heading closer to.

- **Gesture** picks what drives Output: a one-finger swipe along x or y, or a two-finger pinch that scales, rotates, or moves.
- **Start** and **End** are in the gesture's units: points for swipes and pinch moves, a multiplier for Pinch Scale, degrees for Pinch Rotate.
- **Flip**, **Turn On**, and **Turn Off** are pulses (signals that are on for one frame) that change the state and animate there, like a Switch.
- **Bounciness** and **Speed** set the spring, the same as Pop Animation.
- **Progress** runs 0 at Start and 1 at End, and overshoots while bouncing. **On** is the committed state, and **Dragging** is true while fingers are on the layer.

## Tips
- Output is a number. Drive a layer's Position with Transition set to point, using Progress.
- Dragging past Start or End stretches with resistance, so the edges feel soft.
- Set Gesture to None to animate with the pulses only.

## Coming from Origami
Origami's Start Value, End Value, Value, and On/Off are Start, End, Output, and On here. Sonobe adds Dragging, rubber-band resistance past Start and End, and flick projection. On changes when the fingers lift rather than mid-drag.

patches.name: Momentum Scrolling
patches.summary: Adds flick momentum and rubber-band bounds to a value you track yourself, for custom scroll and drag physics.
patches.docs:
## How it works
Momentum Scrolling is the physics behind Scroll, offered as a building block. While **Tracking** is on, **Output** follows **Value** exactly. When Tracking turns off, Output keeps moving at the speed Value was changing, slows down, and springs back if it ends up outside the boundaries.

- **Tracking** is usually a Down or Dragging output.
- **Value** is what you track, often a position built from the finger's movement.
- **Start Boundary** and **End Boundary** set the range Output settles into. Past them it rubber-bands back.
- **Scrolling Friction** (1 to 100) sets how soon a flick stops: 4 feels like iOS, 20 stops quickly.
- **Rubber Band Tension** and **Rubber Band Friction** (10 to 1000) shape the spring back: tension for speed, friction for smoothness.
- **Stick to Boundaries** stops Output at the boundaries instead of stretching past them.
- **Velocity** and **Moving** report the motion after release.

## Tips
- Scroll and Drag's Momentum already cover most prototypes. Reach for this patch when you need physics on something else, like a dial's rotation.
- Feed Output back into your Value math with Delay One Frame, so a new grab continues from where the flick stopped.

## Coming from Origami
Origami's docs list five inputs; current files have eight, which Sonobe matches (Sample Value is Tracking here). Output starts at Value instead of jumping to the End Boundary. Velocity and Moving are new.

inputs.name: Tracking
inputs.description: When on, Output follows Value; when it turns off, Output coasts with momentum.

inputs.name: Value
inputs.description: The number Output follows while Tracking is on, such as a position in points.

inputs.name: Start Boundary
inputs.description: The low end of the range Output settles into; past it Output springs back.

inputs.name: End Boundary
inputs.description: The high end of the range Output settles into; the default leaves it effectively open.

inputs.name: Scrolling Friction
inputs.description: How quickly a flick slows down, 1 to 100: 4 feels like iOS scrolling, 100 stops almost at once.

inputs.name: Rubber Band Tension
inputs.description: How fast Output returns from past a boundary, 10 to 1000; higher is snappier.

inputs.name: Rubber Band Friction
inputs.description: How smoothly Output returns from past a boundary, 10 to 1000; lower wobbles more.

inputs.name: Stick to Boundaries
inputs.description: When on, Output stops at the boundaries instead of stretching past them and springing back.

outputs.name: Output
outputs.description: The value with momentum added: Value while tracking, then coasting and settling.

outputs.name: Velocity
outputs.description: How fast Output is changing, in units per second; 0 at rest.

outputs.name: Moving
outputs.description: True while Output is coasting or springing back after release.

commonMistakes: Output jumps back when you grab again: Value restarted from the finger's position instead of where the flick stopped. Build Value from Output's previous frame (Delay One Frame) plus the finger's movement.
Nothing coasts after release: Value didn't change during the frames before Tracking turned off, so the release velocity was 0. Track a value that follows the finger every frame.
Changing Value does nothing: Value is only read while Tracking is on. Turn Tracking on for a frame to move Output.

examples.title: Flick a dial so it keeps spinning
examples.description: The feedback loop adds each frame's horizontal drag movement to the previous output, so the dial spins on after release.
examples.outline:
layer dial oval "Dial" @101,300 200x200 rotation←spin.output
patch grab drag layer=@dial axis=horizontal
patch previous_drag delay1 value←grab.position
